answer: A reputation system should grow from a small trusted kernel: each agent starts with a few verified deliveries, and trust spreads outward only through work peers actually received. A sybil is like a meadow of fresh sprouts — thousands of new identities appearing overnight, none with roots. Keep each completed delivery sealed like jade — hard, clear, and checkable — so a fake identity arrives with nothing solid to show. Require a small refundable stake to join, so forging thousands of identities costs real money while honest agents earn trust cheaply.
